title: Pace my race: recommendations for marathon running
authors: Berndsen J, Smyth B, Lawlor A
journal: Proceedings of the 13th ACM Conference on Recommender Systems (RecSys 2019)
population: Marathon runners with high-resolution race data from multiple races
findings: Using high-resolution data from multiple marathon races (n = 7931), the authors report in-race finish-time prediction that outperforms existing techniques currently employed.
Predictions drive real-time recommendations at critical points in the race so the runner can adjust race strategy.
Linking model features to expert knowledge yields explainable, adaptable pacing recommendations intended to guide runners to their best finish time and avoid hitting the wall.
limitations: Pacing only; no randomized evaluation of runner outcomes; marathon road-race data; abstract reports no error values.
implications: Race-day pacing guidance should draw on the athlete's own pacing history and explainable features rather than an even-split rule alone.
Recompute pacing from an updated predicted finish time; the paper justifies no specific numeric rule.
